subject: Social Habits
title: Our celebration
objectives: Children will show Year learning through games and a class celebration.
Teachers will complete every child’s end-of-year record and transition note.
content: Revising feelings and bravery, safety and helping, and celebrating the year with end-of-year records and a transition note.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and joyful; observe quietly; record what children can do; invite parents to the celebration; complete the transition note honestly for the Nursery 1 teacher; handle any safeguarding or welfare concern through the school’s policy and not through the transition note alone.
learnerActivities: Show learning from the year through games and a class celebration.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s end-of-year social learning and complete the transition note.
expectedOutcomes: Takes part confidently in familiar routines and games.
Each child has an end-of-year observation record.

lessons.title: Revising feelings and bravery
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will revisit feelings, calming, trying and teamwork through games.
successCriteria: Names a feeling and uses a calming idea
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about feelings, bravery, teamwork, helpers, safety, gratitude, culture and independence this year.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we play our favourite feelings and trying games."
teacherActivities: Play show me a feeling with the feelings cards.
Practise slow breathing with a teddy.
Try stacking cups and say I can try.
learnerActivities: Child tries and says I can try.
Child lifts the cloth with friends.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play show me a feeling with the feelings cards. Children: Child shows a feeling face.
Step 2. Teacher: Practise slow breathing with a teddy. Children: Child breathes slowly.
Step 3. Teacher: Try stacking cups and say I can try. Children: Child tries and says I can try.
Step 4. Teacher: Play the cloth game together. Children: Child lifts the cloth with friends.

practical.title: Feelings and trying games
steps: Children play each for four minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area closely and keep floors clear. Stop any game that upsets a child.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child and use one game.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a calming game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you say before you try?

lessons.conclusion: Take a slow breath and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep naming feelings and praising trying.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit feelings, calming, trying and teamwork through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising safety and helping
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will revisit road safety, safe grown-ups, helpers and thanks through games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about feelings, bravery, teamwork, helpers, safety, gratitude, culture and independence this year.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we play our safety and helper games."
teacherActivities: Play stop and go on a chalk road.
Show the safe hand chart and name safe grown-ups.
Say thank you to a helper.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play stop and go on a chalk road. Children: Child stops and goes.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the safe hand chart and name safe grown-ups. Children: Child names a safe grown-up.
Step 3. Teacher: Play helpers with hats. Children: Child plays a helper.
Step 4. Teacher: Say thank you to a helper. Children: Child says thank you.

practical.title: Safety and helper games
steps: Children play each for four minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and use a closed safe space. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child and hold hands.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the road helper.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do at the kerb?

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep practising safety and thanking helpers.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit road safety, safe grown-ups, helpers and thanks through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Year-end stations
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s end-of-year social learning at play stations.
successCriteria: Shows manners, feelings, teamwork and independence
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about feelings, bravery, teamwork, helpers, safety, gratitude, culture and independence this year.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we play at six stations and show what we know."
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: manners, feelings, teamwork, safety, helping and independence.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: manners, feelings, teamwork, safety, helping and independence. Children: Children rotate every three minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Social stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep floors clear and use large safe toys only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: uses manners; names feelings and calms with help; works with others; follows safety rules; helps; does self-help tasks.

expectedOutcomes: Shows familiar social skills at stations
lessons.conclusion: Say well done to everyone and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite game at home during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s end-of-year social learning at play stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Class celebration
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will celebrate the year with songs and games and show their work to visitors.
successCriteria: Shows something they enjoyed to an adult
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about feelings, bravery, teamwork, helpers, safety, gratitude, culture and independence this year.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate our year. Let us sing our favourite songs."
teacherActivities: Sing favourite songs and rhymes with actions.
Invite children to show their work to a visitor or parent.
Give each child a sticker or certificate and say their name.
learnerActivities: Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite songs and rhymes with actions. Children: Children sing and do actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Invite children to show their work to a visitor or parent. Children: Child shows their work.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or certificate and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.

practical.title: Celebration circle
steps: Sit in a circle with visitors.
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Supervise visitors and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and share their work together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s end-of-year social record from the year’s observations. Record the child’s strengths and a next step for Nursery 1.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you in Nursery 1."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep practising kind habits during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "celebrate the year with songs and games and show their work to visitors" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Transition note and records
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will complete a transition note for each child for the Nursery 1 teacher.
successCriteria: Records what each child can do
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about feelings, bravery, teamwork, helpers, safety, gratitude, culture and independence this year.
lessons.starter: Today the children enjoy free play with familiar materials while the teacher completes the transition notes.
teacherActivities: Set out free play with blocks, a play house, books and a play market.
Review each child’s three term records and portfolio.
Complete the note: strengths, friendships, feelings, routines and next steps.
learnerActivities: Children play while the teacher reviews.
Children play and talk with the helper.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set out free play with blocks, a play house, books and a play market. Children: Children play freely and happily.
Step 2. Teacher: Review each child’s three term records and portfolio. Children: Children play while the teacher reviews.
Step 3. Teacher: Complete the note: strengths, friendships, feelings, routines and next steps. Children: Children play and talk with the helper.

practical.title: Free play and records
steps: Set out four play areas with a helper.
The teacher reviews records at a quiet table.
The teacher completes each transition note.
practical.safety: A second adult must supervise play while the teacher completes the notes. Keep all areas safe and tidy.

differentiation.support: Offer familiar toys and a helper nearby.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to help a friend tidy up.

assessment.method: Write for each child: how they settle, relate to others, manage feelings, follow routines, look after themselves and keep safe; their interests; any support needed; and a next step. Use the four-level scale and facts you have seen, and pass any welfare concern to the safeguarding lead separately.

questions.question: What do you like to play?
What did you enjoy this year?

expectedOutcomes: Has a transition note for each child
lessons.conclusion: Tidy up together and say goodbye to the year.
lessons.homeConnection: Share the end-of-year report with your child and keep practising kind habits.
